cues.text: Did you make notes while you were watching the performances of Romeo and Juliet, Gemma?
GEMMA: Yes, I did. I found it quite hard though. I kept getting too involved in the play.
ED: Me too. I ended up not taking notes. I wrote down my impressions when I got home.
Do you mind if I check a few things with you? In case l've missed anything.
And l've also got some questions about our assignment.
GEMMA: No, it's good to talk things through. I may have missed things too. ED: OK great.
So first of all, I'm not sure how much information we should include in our reviews.
GEMMA: Right. Well, I don't think we need to describe what happens.
Especially as Romeo and Juliet is one of Shakespeare's most well-known plays.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: Yeah, everyone knows the story.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: In an essay we'd focus on the poetry and Shakespeare's use of imagery etc., but that

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: isn't really relevant in a review.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: We're supposed to focus on how effective this particular production is. GEMMA: Mmm.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: We should say what made it a success or a failure.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: And part of that means talking about the emotional impact the performance had on us.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: I think that's important. GEMMA: Yes.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: And we should definitely mention how well the director handled important bits of the play

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: — like when Romeo climbs onto Juliet's balcony.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: And the fight between Mercutio and Tybalt. GEMMA Yes.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: It would also be interesting to mention the theatre space and how the director used it

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: but I don't think we'll have space in 800 words. ED: No. OK.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: That all sounds quite straightforward.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: So what about The Emporium Theatre’s production of the play?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA I thought some things worked really well but there were some problems too. ED: Yeah.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: What about the set, for example?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA I think it was visually really stunning.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: I'd say that was probably the most memorable thing about this production.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: You're right.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: The set design was really amazing, but actually I have seen similar ideas used in other

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: productions. GEMMA What about the lighting?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: Some of the scenes were so dimly lit it was quite hard to see. ED: I didn't dislike it.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: It helped to change the mood of the quieter scenes. GEMMA That's a good point.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: What did you think of the costumes?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA 1 was a bit surprised by the contemporary dress, I must say.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: Yeah — I think it worked well, but I had assumed it would be more conventional.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA Me too.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: I liked the music at the beginning and I thought the musicians were brilliant, but I

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: thought they were wasted because the music didn't have much impact in Acts 2 and 3.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: Yes —that was a shame.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA One problem with this production was that the actors didn't deliver the lines that

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: well. They were speaking too fast.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: It was a problem I agree, but I thought it was because they weren't speaking.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: loudly enough — especially at key points in the play.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA I actually didn't have a problem with that.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: It's been an interesting experience watching different versions of Romeo and Juliet,

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: hasn't it? GEMMA Definitely. It’s made me realise how relevant the play still is.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: Right.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: I mean a lot's changed since Shakespeare's time, but in many ways nothing's changed.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: There are always disagreements and tension between teenagers and their parents.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA Yes, that's something all young people can relate to — more than the violence and

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: the extreme emotions in the play. ED: How did you find watching it in translation?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA Really interesting.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: I expected to find it more challenging, but I could follow the story pretty well.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: I stopped worrying about not being able to understand all the words and focused on

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: the actors' expressions. The ending was pretty powerful. GEMMA Yes.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: That somehow intensified the emotion for me.

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: Did you know Shakespeare's been translated into more languages than any other writer?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: GEMMA: What's the reason for his international appeal, do you think?

cues.speaker: ED
cues.text: ED: I was reading that it's because his plays are about basic themes that people 104
